title: Petra and the Gravity
premise: Dominic Quintana has spent nine years alone on Relay Station Petra, tending a beacon whose original commissioning orders were scrubbed from every archive. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew aged backward into children who remember futures that haven't happened yet, Dominic realizes the beacon is a lighthouse for something coming through the jump window—and that she was placed here to be its last witness. As two rival fleets converge on Petra, each believing Dominic holds the key to the beacon's true purpose, she fabricates an authority she doesn't have, inventing orders from a dead admiralty to keep them from firing on each other. The lie works too well: both fleets obey her invented command structure, and when the window opens and the beacon's makers finally answer, Dominic must choose between confessing her fraud and letting the fleets destroy each other over a truth neither can survive. She confesses—and discovers the beacon was built for exactly this: not to guide ships home, but to find one person willing to carry the weight of a decision no committee could make.
about_author: Ivo Ishikawa is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years maintaining automated navigation beacons in the North Pacific before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness as a form of competence, and they write from a converted signal station on Hokkaido's coast.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine maintenance cycle establishes her solitary life aboard Petra: calibrating the beacon, talking to the station AI, logging hours nobody reads. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by the question of why the station exists at all.

chapters.title: Commission Unknown
chapters.summary: Dominic digs into station archives after a beacon anomaly—a pulse sent toward deep space, not from it. Every founding record is redacted or missing. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: first crack of unease; invisibility begins to feel like design.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: Long-range sensors catch a ship decelerating from interstellar space—the Halcyon, lost forty years ago. POV: Dominic, with dread building. Emotional beat: hope curdling into fear, because nothing returns unchanged.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Dominic docks the Halcyon's shuttle and finds its crew aged backward—adults now children under ten, physically and neurologically. They recognize her. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: horror and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: What Mira Remembers
chapters.summary: A girl named Mira, formerly the Halcyon's captain, describes events that haven't occurred—including Dominic's own death. POV alternates Dominic/Mira. Emotional beat: vertigo; the future arrives as testimony.

chapters.title: Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Both the Concord fleet and the Meridian flotilla detect the Halcyon's return and set course for Petra, each claiming jurisdiction. POV: brief fleet-side interludes via intercepted comms. Emotional beat: Dominic watches her isolation end as a siege begins.

chapters.title: The First Lie
chapters.summary: Concord hails demanding the beacon's codes. Dominic, unqualified to refuse, improvises: she cites emergency authority from a defunct admiralty directive she fabricates on the spot. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of the first lie holding.

chapters.title: Acting Authority
chapters.summary: Meridian arrives; Dominic extends the same fabricated directive to them, positioning herself as neutral custodian. Both fleets stand down—for now. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the strange power of being believed.

chapters.title: Caretaker
chapters.summary: Dominic cares for the Halcyon children while managing two suspicious captains. Mira warns her the lie will be tested. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: motherhood-by-circumstance; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: A Concord records officer cross-references Dominic's cited directive and finds it doesn't exist—but says nothing, wanting leverage. POV: the officer, Voss. Emotional beat: menace; the lie has a witness.

chapters.title: The Beacon Speaks
chapters.summary: The beacon transmits unprompted—a structured message aimed at the jump window, counting down. Both fleets interpret it as evidence of alien contact. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: awe weaponized; her fiction now competes with a real mystery.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Voss privately offers to bury his findings if Dominic delivers the beacon to Concord. POV: Voss, then Dominic. Emotional beat: corruption's quiet arithmetic—power offered as protection.

chapters.title: Mira's Second Memory
chapters.summary: Mira recalls more of the reversed timeline: in it, Dominic lied differently, and everyone died. She begs her to change course. POV: Mira. Emotional beat: guilt inherited from a future that may still happen.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Meridian detects Concord's private channel to Petra; accusations fly. Dominic issues her boldest invented order—a joint quarantine—to prevent open fire. It barely holds. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: exhaustion; leadership as continuous improvisation.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dominic finds a sealed compartment keyed to her biometrics: the station's founders chose her lineage deliberately, training generations of Quintanas unknowingly. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: identity upended—invisibility was inheritance.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: The jump window begins; the beacon's makers transmit an actual arrival signature. Fleets arm. Voss moves to seize the station. POV: multiple, rapid cuts. Emotional beat: everything converges at once.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Dominic broadcasts the truth—her fraud, her forged authority, her ignorance—to both fleets, betting honesty can do what the lie couldn't. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: liberation and exposure; the fall before the catch.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Wanted
chapters.summary: The makers' message resolves: the beacon tests whether someone will claim responsibility without claiming reward. Dominic passed years ago. The fleets, shamed, stand down. POV: Mira interpreting, Dominic living it. Emotional beat: meaning arriving late but fully.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss, exposed, must decide whether to report the truth or protect the peace it produced. He chooses silence, taking the corruption theme to its redemptive edge. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: complicity transformed into grace.

chapters.title: Passage
chapters.summary: The makers' vessel passes through without stopping, leaving the children restored to their proper ages as it goes—time owed, returned. POV: Dominic watching. Emotional beat: grief and wonder braided; some gifts can't be kept.

chapters.title: Command
chapters.summary: Both fleets formally offer Dominic real authority over Petra and the window. She accepts—not as the person she pretended to be, but as the one the pretending revealed. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: identity integrated; the mask becomes the face.

chapters.title: Petra and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Dominic, Mira, and the rebuilt crew keep the beacon, now understood: gravity isn't what pulls you down, but what holds things together. She logs the hours, and this time someone reads them. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: earned solitude, no longer lonely.
